title: Generalizable and Actionable Parts Pose Estimation with Symmetry Annotation-Free Learning Strategy
claim: A two-stage pipeline generates candidate poses, then refines them and handles symmetry through a dedicated module built on a custom layer.
layout: 3 regions: top stage 1, bottom stage 2, right legend and module zoom-in; left-to-right
description: A wide, color-coded system diagram with three zones. The top green band, Stage 1: Candidate Generation, flows left to right. It starts from an object point cloud and goes through segmentation to a part point cloud. A backbone then produces features F^pc, which are concatenated with n_i and passed to a Candidate Net. That outputs quaternion candidates q1..qk. The bottom blue band, Stage 2: Refinement and Symmetry, takes the quaternions through a Quaternion Encoder and a small network to get Δq. These give corrected candidates Q^correct, drawn as coordinate frames. They are aggregated into q^final. A Symmetry Net predicts symmetry planes, and an equivalent transformation produces equivalent rotations, shown as red arrows on a point cloud. On the right, a legend and a gold zoomed-in HyperS3 layer diagram with KNN, Conv, STE and ORL blocks. Dashed lines link the backbone to the HyperS3 detail.
caption: Overview of our framework. First, we construct a backbone with our designed S3 hyperspherical (HyperS3) layer to extract point cloud feature. Then, we generate quaternion candidates and refine each on the hyperspherical manifold of quaternion S3. To better cope with the multi-hypothesis caused by symmetry, we additionally design a self-adaptive network to estimate the symmetry axes or planes, based on which we generate the corresponding equivalent solutions later. Finally, we aggregate all refined candidates and apply an additional refinement step, yielding qfinal.
abstract: Urgently needed generalizable robot object interaction and manipulation requires high-quality Cross-Category object perception. As a pioneer of this area, Generalizable and Actionable Parts (GAParts) understanding has attracted increasing attention from relevant researchers. However, most recent works either have insufficient design regarding the symmetry issue or require rich symmetry annotation, which severely impedes precise GAPart pose estimation in data-lacking scenarios. In this paper, we propose SAFAG, a novel Symmetry Annotation-Free framework for Generalizable and Actionable Parts Pose Estimation. Specifically, we suggest a stepwise refinement two-stage framework for candidate-to-final quaternion regression, and tackle the symmetry prediction as a probability distribution problem with self-supervised learning strategy. The experimental results demonstrate the superior performance and robustness of our SAFAG. We believe that our work has the enormous potential to be applied in many areas of embodied AI system.
